text:
Connor McMichael's first season in St. Louis, after 315 games in Washington, has been quiet: 2 goals and 9 points in 20 games, and no goals in his last ten. On Nov. 12 he finally got one to count, sort of, scoring in the eighth round of a shootout as the Blues beat Utah 1-0.

The bigger story is around him. St. Louis has scored 8.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with McMichael on the ice, and that has cost him points. Our numbers flag him as due. His own finishing is cold too: 7.4% shooting against a usual range of 9.6% to 14.1%.

His game is built on speed and transition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries last season, with 60% of his shots coming off the rush. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level in 2025-26 because of the defensive cost: opponents got 0.18 more expected goals per 60 with him out there, bottom 5% of forwards. Bounces turn; that number is the one we'd watch.
headline: McMichael's quiet St. Louis start has two causes
